questions.q: Which button on the Users list page lets you create up to ten users at once?
options: New User
Reset Password(s)
Add Multiple Users
Freeze
questions.explain: Add Multiple Users opens a streamlined form for creating up to 10 user records in one pass.

questions.q: Where does almost every Salesforce admin task begin?
options: Setup, reached from the gear icon
The Developer Console
The AppExchange
A third-party IDE
questions.explain: Setup, opened from the gear icon in the top right of any org, is where configuration work happens.

questions.q: How do permission sets and permission set groups relate to a user's profile?
options: They replace the profile entirely
They only ever add access on top of the profile, never remove it
They can only be assigned instead of a profile, not alongside one
They override and can revoke profile-granted permissions
questions.explain: A user's profile sets the baseline; permission sets and permission set groups only add to that baseline, as covered in the next two lessons.

questions.q: Where does Delegated Administration live in Setup?
options: In the Security Controls section, alongside Sharing Settings and Session Settings
Inside Object Manager, under each object's Field Dependencies page
Inside the Profiles list, as a checkbox on each profile
In the App Manager, as a type of connected app
questions.explain: Delegated Administration is found in Setup's Security Controls section, the same area as Sharing Settings and Session Settings — reflecting that it's a security boundary.

questions.q: Where in Setup's navigation does Permission Set Groups sit relative to Permission Sets?
options: Under Company Information, unrelated to Permission Sets
In the same Administration section, right above Permission Sets
Only accessible through the Developer Console
Under Email Administration
questions.explain: Permission Set Groups is grouped with Permission Sets, Profiles, and Users under Setup's Administration section.

questions.q: Where does a user go to switch between apps they have access to?
options: The Setup gear icon
The App Launcher, opened from the grid icon in the top-left of Lightning Experience
Object Manager
The Profile edit page
questions.explain: The App Launcher shows every app a user has access to, plus a searchable list of individual tabs and items beyond their current app.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe Company Information as a page that affects "almost every setting you'll touch from here forward"?
options: Because it is the only page an administrator is allowed to edit
Because several settings on it — locale, time zone, fiscal year, currency — are org-wide defaults that other features and pages read from
Because every other Setup page requires Company Information to be edited first
Because it controls which users can log in to the org
questions.explain: Company Information holds org-wide defaults (locale, time zone, fiscal year) that ripple outward into user records, reports, and forecasts, which is why it's the starting point for this chapter.

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe console-style apps as the default shape for Service Cloud-style work?
options: Because console apps are required by Salesforce for any object with cases
Because support agents constantly jump between related records and need quick tools without losing their current screen — exactly what console navigation plus a utility bar provides
Because Standard navigation is being deprecated
Because console apps don't require a Navigation Items configuration
questions.explain: The lesson explains that the combination of console navigation (subtabs) and a utility bar (docked tools) matches the high-volume, multi-record nature of support work.

questions.q: Where does an admin configure which tabs appear by default in a Lightning app, and in what order?
options: The Navigation Items step of that app in App Manager
The Object Manager's Page Layouts page
Each user's individual profile
The Lightning App Builder's Record Detail component
questions.explain: Navigation Items is the App Manager wizard step with Available Items and Selected Items columns, where the admin sets the default tab set and order.

questions.q: Among Org Default, App Default, and App-Record Type-Profile assignment levels, which one wins when more than one applies to the same user?
options: Org Default always wins regardless of other assignments
Whichever was created first wins
App Default always overrides App, Record Type, and Profile
The most specific level — App, Record Type, and Profile — overrides the other two
questions.explain: The resolution order is: Org Default is shown unless overridden by App Default, which is itself overridden by the more specific App, Record Type, and Profile assignment.

questions.q: In a field dependency between Issue Type and Issue Detail, which role does Issue Type play?
options: The dependent field, filtered by Issue Detail
The controlling field — what the user picks first, filtering Issue Detail's options
Neither; Issue Type is unrelated to the dependency
A global value set shared across objects
questions.explain: The lesson's example sets Issue Type as the controlling field and Issue Detail as the dependent field whose values get filtered.

questions.q: Why does a multi-select picklist or long text field show up differently in the History related list than a standard picklist?
options: Those field types aren't trackable at all
They require Field Audit Trail to track at all
They only record that a change happened and who made it — not the specific old/new values, since those field types are too large to log value-by-value
They record the change twice, once for each selected value
questions.explain: Multi-select picklists and long text fields are tracked differently: Salesforce logs that a change happened and who made it, but not the specific old/new values.

questions.q: A user can see a field as a column in a list view, but typing it into the list's search box returns nothing. What's the most likely explanation?
options: The list view is broken and needs to be rebuilt
List views only support searching the first column
The user doesn't have field-level security access to that field
That field isn't indexed for in-list search — a filter or sort on that field would work instead
questions.explain: Visible in a list view's columns and searchable via in-list search are two different things — some fields (often system fields) simply aren't indexed for in-list search, which is exactly what Salesforce's own tooltip warns about.

questions.q: When creating a new picklist field, what choice does the field wizard offer regarding global value sets?
options: There is no such choice — all picklists are global value sets automatically
The choice only appears on multi-select picklists
Only System Administrators can choose to use a global value set
Enter values specific to this field, or use a global picklist value set that's shared across objects
questions.explain: The field wizard offers 'Enter values, with each value separated by a new line' (an ordinary picklist) or 'Use a global picklist value set,' which points the field at a value set defined once and shared.

questions.q: Where does an admin add or configure a related list on a Lightning Record Page?
options: Lightning App Builder, as a draggable component pointed at a related object
Object Manager → Validation Rules
Setup → Profiles → Related List Access
The Report Builder's field selector
questions.explain: A related list is a component in Lightning App Builder, placed on the record page and pointed at a specific related object, with its own settings panel.

questions.q: After creating a routing address, what has to happen in your real email system for Email-to-Case to actually work?
options: Nothing — Salesforce reads the real inbox directly without any forwarding
The real address must be deleted
You must forward incoming mail from the real address to the generated *.case.salesforce.com address
Your email system needs a Salesforce-signed SSL certificate installed
questions.explain: Salesforce never reads your real mailbox directly — you configure your email system to forward messages to the generated email services address, which is what Salesforce actually receives.

questions.q: What does the 'Don't Share' default activity sharing setting do?
options: Prevents synced activities from ever being created
Deletes synced activities after 30 days
Blocks Einstein Activity Capture from syncing emails entirely
Keeps synced activities private to their owner unless the user chooses to share one individually
questions.explain: 'Don't Share' is the more conservative default — other users won't see a synced activity on a record unless the owner explicitly shares it.

questions.q: Where does an admin define a new Custom Notification Type?
options: Setup → Notification Builder → Custom Notifications
Object Manager → Feed Tracking
Setup → Email-to-Case Settings
The Chatter Group creation screen
questions.explain: Custom Notification Types are created from Setup under Notification Builder → Custom Notifications.

questions.q: What are the three post types available in the Chatter publisher?
options: Post, Poll, and Question
Email, Task, and Event
Note, File, and Link
Update, Alert, and Reminder
questions.explain: The Chatter publisher offers Post (a plain update), Poll (a quick vote), and Question (a post others can answer).

questions.q: What is the practical difference between a letterhead and a template?
options: A letterhead is the reusable branding shell (logo, header/footer, colors); a template is a specific email that applies a letterhead and adds its own subject and body
There is no difference — the terms are interchangeable in Salesforce
A letterhead only works in Salesforce Classic, never in Lightning
A template can only use one letterhead ever, with no way to change it later
questions.explain: Separating the reusable branding (letterhead) from the specific email content (template) means updating the letterhead once updates every template built on it.

questions.q: What do Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes include?
options: Metadata only — no production records
All production data and all metadata
Only production data, with no metadata
A sampled subset of production data via a template
questions.explain: Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes copy configuration (metadata) only — objects, fields, layouts, flows, Apex — with no actual records.

questions.q: What replaced the older 'Critical Updates' console in Salesforce Setup?
options: Release Updates, which includes more detailed information about upcoming changes than the old console did
Field Audit Trail
Setup Audit Trail
Change Sets
questions.explain: Release Updates is the modern replacement for the Critical Updates console, with more detail about each change, step-by-step actions, and a test run option.

questions.q: Why does the lesson treat documentation as a discipline rather than an afterthought?
options: Because Salesforce requires a documentation field to be filled in before any change can save
Because undocumented changes are automatically reverted after 90 days
Because documentation is graded as part of the Salesforce Certified Administrator exam
Because a setting changed with no note of why becomes a trap for whoever looks at it later — including a future version of the same admin who has forgotten the context
questions.explain: The lesson's point is practical, not procedural: the cost of a short documentation habit is near zero in the moment, and the payoff is real the first time someone (possibly the same admin, later) needs to understand why a setting exists.

questions.q: What does Setup Audit Trail record?
options: Changes to record field values, like Opportunity Stage or Account Industry
Configuration changes made in Setup — permission sets, profiles, security settings, Apex classes, Flow versions, and more — with who made each change and when
Every report and dashboard a user has ever viewed
The content of every email sent through the org
questions.explain: Setup Audit Trail tracks configuration changes in Setup, not record data — each entry shows the Date, User, and Action for a change like a permission set edit or security setting update.

questions.q: What does the 'Run specified tests' option do when deploying a change set?
options: Runs every test in the org, including managed package tests
Runs no tests at all, regardless of environment
Automatically generates new test classes for any included Apex
Runs only the test classes you explicitly name, which must meet a 75% code coverage requirement for the included Apex
questions.explain: Run Specified Tests limits execution to named test classes, but Salesforce still requires at least 75% code coverage on the deployed Apex.
